First, we express $y$ as a composite function

$$
y=\operatorname{tan}⁡u,\,u=3{x}^{4}-5.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}={sec}^{2}⁡u,\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=12{x}^{3}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡u\cdot 12{x}^{3} \\  & =12{x}^{3}{sec}^{2}⁡u \\  & =12{x}^{3}{sec}^{2}⁡(3{x}^{4}-5).\end{aligned}
$$
